publication_revisions.abstract: We report spectroscopic observations with Keck/DEIMOS of old (~1-9 years post-explosion) type II supernovae detected by the Rubin/LSST, some of which are powered by on-going CSM interaction.

publication_revisions.abstract: We report the prior identification of late-time mid-infrared rebrightening in SN 2020jfv and SN 2020izc with WISE/NEOWISE, more than two years before their optical rebrightening in LSST EDP2. Persistent MIR emission beyond 1000 days, together with late-time Hα emission in SN 2020izc and UV excess in SN 2020jfv, confirms ongoing circumstellar-medium interaction. These results demonstrate the power of infrared selection for identifying long-lived interacting supernovae and motivate continued late-time IR monitoring in the LSST era.
publication_revisions.authors_text: Kohki Uno (Columbia), Kishalay De (Columbia), Geoffrey Mo (Caltech/Carnegie Observatories) , Viraj Karambelkar (Columbia) report on behalf of a larger team
